standard_prerequisites.name: Ideals of closed immersions of algebraic spaces and the factorisation criterion
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma labelled spaces-morphisms-lemma-closed-immersion-ideals (canonical Stacks tag 03MB); invoked at proof lines 2383-2386 and again at 2388-2390
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies b^#(b^{-1}I) contained in J from the commutativity of the diagram, and the criterion that b factors through Z' once b^#(b^{-1}(I^2)) = 0.

core_obligations: Work inside the construction of Z': let U contained in X be the open subspace used to build Z', so that Z is a closed subspace of U cut out by the quasi-coherent ideal I; since T and T' have the same underlying topological space, the image of T' under b lies in U, so b may be regarded as a morphism into U (proof lines 2372-2379).

Compare ideals: let J contained in O_{T'} be the square-zero quasi-coherent ideal cutting out T; the commutativity of the diagram gives b^#(b^{-1}I) contained in J, and since T contained in T' is a first order thickening, J^2 = 0 and hence b^#(b^{-1}(I^2)) = 0 (proof lines 2380-2388).

Conclude the universal property: the factorisation criterion for closed immersions then gives that b factors through Z', and the resulting map a' : T' -> Z' yields the unique morphism (a', a) of thickenings over X, proving part (1); the author proves only part (1) and leaves the higher order statement to the same pattern (proof lines 2388-2391).
proof_roadmap: Replace X by the open subspace U of the construction and use |T| = |T'| to regard b as a morphism into U (proof lines 2372-2379).
Show b^#(b^{-1}I) is contained in the square-zero ideal J of T and hence b^#(b^{-1}(I^2)) = 0 (proof lines 2380-2388).
Apply the closed-immersion factorisation criterion to obtain a' : T' -> Z', which is the asserted universal property (proof lines 2388-2391).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states the universal property of the first order (and, in part (2), the n-th order) infinitesimal neighbourhood of an immersion i : Z -> X of algebraic spaces: every commutative diagram with a first order thickening T contained in T' over X admits a unique morphism (a', a) : (T contained in T') -> (Z contained in Z') of thickenings over X (statement lines 2342-2368). Compared with its scheme-level counterpart the proof needs one extra input, that a morphism of algebraic spaces whose image lies in an open subspace factors through it, in order to move into the open U of the construction; after that the ideal comparison and the closed-immersion factorisation criterion go through as before (proof lines 2372-2391). The author proves only part (1) and that restriction is reproduced as written. The claim is H2.
